en.welcomeSub: the free encyclopedia that anyone can edit. Featured topic: [[minori-prefecture|Harvest Prefecture]] and its capital, [[harukawa|Springvale]].

featured.title: From today's featured article
featured.text: '''[[harukawa-castle|Springvale Castle]]''' is a hirayama-style Japanese castle on Sagimai Hill in [[harukawa|Springvale]], [[minori-prefecture|Harvest Prefecture]]. It was built between 1603 and 1611 by Asagiri Tadamasa, first lord of the [[asagiri-clan|Asagiri clan]], and gave the city its castle town. The original five-tiered keep burned after a lightning strike on 15 June 1749 and was rebuilt by 1755, only to be demolished in 1874 when the castle buildings were sold off. The present keep, a reinforced-concrete reconstruction opened on 3 November 1966, was paid for in large part by citizens' donations collected under Mayor [[tetsuo-saeki|Tetsuo Saeki]]. Two original buildings survive: the Tatsumi Turret of 1609 and the Sagimai Gate of 1757. The castle grounds host the [[minori-prefectural-museum-of-art|Harvest Prefectural Museum of Art]] and, every October, the processions of the [[harukawa-lantern-festival|Springvale Lantern Festival]].

dyk.title: Did you know ...
items: ... that [[minori-prefecture|Harvest Prefecture]] has officially written its name in hiragana since 1971 because the kanji 実野 was so often misread?
... that the oldest surviving building of [[harukawa-castle|Springvale Castle]] is 357 years older than the castle's keep?
... that the potter [[hanae-ishizuka|Hanae Ishizuka]] (''pictured: a jar with kawasuji brushwork'') needed 214 test firings to recreate the "mist glaze" of [[harukawa-ware|Springvale ware]]?
... that the [[tsukikage|Comet]] limited express is built for 120 km/h but never runs faster than 95 km/h?
... that in 1688 every farming household in Harvest was ordered to plant three [[yuzu-cultivation-in-minori|yuzu trees]]?
... that [[mount-tsukimi|Mount Moonview]] lost two metres of height in a 2014 survey?

news.title: In the news
items: Preparations are under way for the 282nd '''[[harukawa-lantern-festival|Springvale Lantern Festival]]''' (''lanterns pictured''), to be held on 10–11 October.

The [[harukawa-railway|Springvale Railway]] revises its timetables on 14 November: the [[tsukikage|Comet]] will also stop at Trailhead, and [[bayside-line|Bayside Line]] trains will run every 15 minutes on weekday middays.
Mayor Takuya Hirose seeks a third term in the [[harukawa|Springvale]] mayoral election on 8 November.
The [[minori-prefectural-museum-of-art|Harvest Prefectural Museum of Art]] opens a retrospective of the potter [[hanae-ishizuka|Hanae Ishizuka]], running until 23 November.
Tourist visitors to [[harukawa|Springvale]] reached a record 6.5 million in 2025, according to [[economy-of-harukawa|city figures]].
The green [[yuzu-cultivation-in-minori|yuzu]] harvest ends in Harvest Prefecture; picking of yellow fruit begins this month.

onThisDay.title: On this day
onThisDay.lead: Events in the history of [[harukawa|Springvale]] and [[minori-prefecture|Harvest Prefecture]]:
items: '''1739''' – The Great Genbun Flood of the [[kagami-river|Mirror River]] killed about 1,140 people in Springvale; the [[harukawa-lantern-festival|Lantern Festival]] began as their memorial the following year.
'''1931''' – The Mirror Valley Railway, today's [[kagami-line|Mirror Line]], reached [[tsukimi-onsen|Moonview Spa]] with the opening of the 2,184-metre [[tsukimi-tunnel|Moonview Tunnel]].
'''2015''' – The Suyama Old Kiln, a 14-chamber climbing kiln of [[harukawa-ware|Springvale ware]], was designated a National Historic Site.

picture.title: Today's featured picture
picture.caption: Floating lanterns on the [[kagami-river|Mirror River]] during the [[harukawa-lantern-festival|Springvale Lantern Festival]]. On the Saturday evening about 12,000 paper lanterns are released just below [[kagami-bridge|Mirror Bridge]] and drift 1.4 km downstream to Shiomi Bridge, where nets collect them. Photograph: Openpedia contributor.

featured.title: 今日の一項目
featured.text: '''[[harukawa-castle|春川城]]'''は、[[minori-prefecture|みのり県]][[harukawa|春川市]]の鷺舞山にある平山城である。1603年から1611年にかけて[[asagiri-clan|朝霧氏]]初代の朝霧忠正が築き、城下町春川の起点となった。五重の天守は1749年6月15日の落雷による火災で焼失し、1755年までに再建されたが、1874年に城内の建物が払い下げられた際に取り壊された。現在の天守は1966年11月3日に完成した鉄筋コンクリート造の復元天守で、[[tetsuo-saeki|佐伯哲夫]]市長のもとで集められた市民の寄付が費用の多くを賄った。1609年の巽櫓と1757年の鷺舞門の2棟が現存する。城跡には[[minori-prefectural-museum-of-art|みのり県立美術館]]があり、毎年10月には[[harukawa-lantern-festival|春川灯籠まつり]]の行列が練り歩く。
featured.more: （[[harukawa-castle|続きを読む]]）最近の一項目：[[harukawa-ware|春川焼]]・[[kagami-line|鏡線]]・[[michiyo-tono|遠野美千代]]

dyk.title: 新しい記事から
items: …[[minori-prefecture|みのり県]]の表記が1971年からひらがなになったのは、「実野」がよく読み間違えられたためである
…[[harukawa-castle|春川城]]で現存する最古の建物は、天守より357年古い
…陶芸家の[[hanae-ishizuka|石塚花枝]]は、[[harukawa-ware|春川焼]]の「霞釉」を再現するまでに214回の試し焼きを重ねた（写真は川筋文の壺）
…特急[[tsukikage|「月影」]]の車両は最高時速120 kmで設計されているが、営業運転では95 kmを超えることがない
…1688年、みのりの農家は一戸あたり3本の[[yuzu-cultivation-in-minori|ユズ]]を植えるよう命じられた
…[[mount-tsukimi|月見山]]の標高は2014年の測量で2 m低くなった
dyk.more: [[harukawa|春川市についてもっと読む]]

news.title: ニュース
items: 第282回'''[[harukawa-lantern-festival|春川灯籠まつり]]'''（写真）が10月10日・11日に開かれる。準備が進んでいる。
[[harukawa-railway|春川鉄道]]は11月14日にダイヤを改正する。特急[[tsukikage|「月影」]]が月見口にも停車し、[[bayside-line|湾岸線]]は平日日中も15分間隔になる。
11月8日の[[harukawa|春川市]]長選挙で、広瀬拓也市長が3選を目指す。
[[minori-prefectural-museum-of-art|みのり県立美術館]]で陶芸家[[hanae-ishizuka|石塚花枝]]の回顧展が始まった。会期は11月23日まで。
2025年の[[harukawa|春川市]]の観光入込客数は過去最多の650万人に達した（[[economy-of-harukawa|市の統計]]）。
みのり県で青ユズの収穫が終わり、今月から黄ユズの収穫が始まる（[[yuzu-cultivation-in-minori|ユズ栽培]]）。

onThisDay.title: 今日は何の日
onThisDay.lead: [[harukawa|春川市]]と[[minori-prefecture|みのり県]]の歴史から
items: '''1739年''' - [[kagami-river|鏡川]]で元文の大洪水が起き、春川で約1,140人が死亡。翌年、犠牲者の供養として[[harukawa-lantern-festival|灯籠流し]]が始まる。
'''1931年''' - 全長2,184 mの[[tsukimi-tunnel|月見トンネル]]の完成により、鏡谷鉄道（現在の[[kagami-line|鏡線]]）が[[tsukimi-onsen|月見温泉]]まで開通。
'''2015年''' - [[harukawa-ware|春川焼]]の14室の登り窯「陶山古窯」が国の史跡に指定される。

en: '''Openpedia''' is a free online encyclopedia written collaboratively by its readers. This copy is a fictional website made for a research study of UniLens, an assistant for people with low vision. Its articles describe the fictional city of [[harukawa|Springvale]] and [[minori-prefecture|Harvest Prefecture]]; the people, places and organisations in them do not exist.

Use the search box at the top of every page to find an article. Suggestions appear as you type; press Enter to see all results. Every article links to related articles, and the categories at the bottom of each article list similar pages. The language link at the top right opens the same page in Japanese.

Openpedia articles cite their sources in numbered footnotes. A statement marked [citation needed] has not yet been supported by a reliable source. To cite an article, give its title, "Openpedia" and the date you read it.
Editing, talk pages and page histories are not available in this copy.
Donations are not collected by this copy of Openpedia. The fundraising banner is part of the study design.
This site sets no cookies and collects no personal data. A small setting in your browser's local storage remembers whether you closed the fundraising banner.
Openpedia makes no guarantee of validity. All content is fictional.
Questions about the study go to the research team that invited you.
